content: Any spatial rotation can be represented as a combination of three principal rotations, also known as Euler angles. These rotations are used to describe the orientation of an object or coordinate system in three-dimensional space. By decomposing a rotation into its principal rotations, it becomes easier to understand and manipulate the orientation of an object.
